documents.generated_document: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Worsening shortness of breath and leg swelling. HPI: The patient is a 72-year-old male, well known to me, presenting today for an urgent add-on visit due to a 4-day history of progressively worsening dyspnea on exertion. He states he can now only walk about 10 feet before having to stop and catch his breath. He also reports worsening orthopnea, requiring 3 pillows to sleep last night compared to his baseline of 1. He has noticed increased swelling in both legs and reports an 8-pound weight gain since his last weigh-in 5 days ago. He denies chest pain, palpitations, syncope, or fever. PMH: HFrEF (last echo 4 months ago showed LVEF 25%), CAD s/p PCI in 2018, CKD stage 3a, Type 2 DM. MEDICATIONS: Entresto 49/51 mg BID, Carvedilol 12.5 mg BID, Furosemide 40 mg daily, Jardiance 10 mg daily, Aspirin 81 mg daily. ROS: Positive for dyspnea, orthopnea, and bilateral lower extremity edema. Negative for chest pain, cough, fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting. PHYSICAL EXAM: Vitals: BP 102/64, HR 94, RR 24, SpO2 90% on room air, Temp 98.2F, Weight 194 lbs (up from 186 lbs). General: Mild respiratory distress at rest, speaking in short sentences. Neck: JVD present to the angle of the mandible at 45 degrees. CV: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, S3 gallop present, no murmurs. Lungs: Bibasilar crackles extending one-third up both lung fields. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema bilaterally extending up to the mid-thighs, warm to touch, pulses 1+ bilaterally. LAB FINDINGS: Point of care testing in clinic today reveals a BNP of 1850 pg/mL (baseline typically 400-500). Stat BMP drawn in clinic shows Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.4), BUN 45, Potassium 4.9, Sodium 134. ASSESSMENT/IMPRESSION: 1. Acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation, severe. 2. Acute kidney injury (AKI) superimposed on CKD stage 3, likely cardiorenal syndrome. PLAN: The patient is currently experiencing a severe decompensation of his HFrEF with concurrent AKI. I had a lengthy discussion with the patient and his daughter regarding the high risk of further decompensation and strongly recommended hospital admission for IV diuresis and close monitoring. The patient adamantly refuses hospitalization at this time and wishes to try aggressive outpatient management. Given his refusal to go to the ER, we will proceed with a high-risk outpatient diuretic strategy. 1. Increase Furosemide to 80 mg PO BID for the next 3 days. 2. Hold Entresto temporarily due to the acute kidney injury and borderline low blood pressure. 3. Hold Jardiance temporarily to avoid further volume depletion compounding the AKI. 4. Strict fluid restriction of less than 1.5 liters per day and strict low sodium diet. 5. Patient is to return to the clinic in 48 hours for a repeat clinical evaluation and stat BMP to monitor his creatinine and potassium levels closely. 6. Strict return precautions provided; patient and daughter verbalized understanding that if his breathing worsens at all tonight, they must call 911 or go directly to the nearest emergency department.
